answer: Temporal work auction. Each new identity must win a paid micro-task whose answer is checked against a cipher the issuer alone solves, so registering costs one verified compute-hour. A staggered release schedule, keyed to a saffron salt value rotated hourly, forces sequential registration and makes bulk creation rent real time. The ledger caps identities per hardware clock cycle, like a lantern with fixed wick. Cloning a thousand agents costs a thousand sequential hours plus task fees, a linear curve that never flattens.
